consumer: The engine's possession predicate (a dialogue/mission has-item check such as player::has_amount / u_has_items over the c4 id) asking 'does the avatar possess a brick of C-4?'
scope: The full possession reach the predicate uses — on-person items INCLUDING recursion into container/pocket contents (and charge counting), not just a flat per-slice surface walk
decisive_source: src/arcopolis_export.cpp::write_carried_items — enumerates only wielded_items(), worn, and inv_const_slice() stacks as raw JSON, a Class-S item dump that does not invoke or reproduce the engine's possession predicate or its container recursion
divergence: A c4 brick stored inside a closed container in the inventory (e.g. inside a duffel bag in a backpack): the engine's has_amount possession check counts it as possessed, but the flat per-stack walk reports only the outer container, so the surface answers 'no' while the true predicate answers 'yes'
